1.
Heard Shri Siddhartha Sinha, learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. for the State.
2.  As per learned col for the applicant, the present applicant has been falsely implicated in the case as he has not committed any offence as alleged in the FIR.
The applicant is in jail since 15.02.2024 in FIR/Crime No.74 of 2022, under Sections 452, 354, 308, 376, 323, 313 of IPC, Police Station Achalganj, District Unnao.

3. Attention has been drawn towards impugned FIR wherein the date of incident is 04.04.2022,
whereas FIR was lodged on 07.04.2022 on the advise of the Advocate.

sentences.text: More or less similar allegations have been levelled against all the accused persons but during investigation it is found that one of the accused persons Ashok was not present on the spot on the date of incident, therefore, final report has been filed against him and against such final report no protest petition has been filed on behalf of complainant/ informant.

Further, against another accused person Gajodhar charge sheet has been filed only under Section 354 I.P.C.
4.

Shri Sinha has submitted that there is no eye-witness account of the incident in question and two alleged eye-witnesses namely, Rupa and Neetu have stated that they have recorded their statement on the basis of information so received from the victim as they have not seen the incident.
Their statement have been enclosed as Annexure nos.17 and 18 to the application.

Shri Sinha has further submitted that as per allegations in the FIR, the victim sustained serious injuries and in those injuries there was bleeding but as per injury report and supplementary injury report, except complaint of pain there was no injury on the body of the victim, not even any contusion.
As per the opinion of the doctor, no injury on the private part of the victim was found and the cause of abortion cannot be explained.

Therefore, Shri Sinha has submitted that entire allegation in the FIR was false,
concocted and misconceived.

5. Shri Sinha has drawn attention of this Court towards Annexure no.15 which is a statement of the victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. on 07.04.2022 wherein she has not levelled any allegation of rape against the accused persons.

In such statement she has admitted that the FIR was written by one Advocate on 07.04.2022, Though in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. on 08.04.2022 the victim has levelled allegation of Section 375 IPC against only Ashok and Vijay.

In both the aforesaid statement recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., the victim has alleged false allegations of beating the victim mercilessly, resultant thereof, she sustained serious injuries.
Though such allegations have not been corroborated with the injury report.
Learned court for the applicant has submitted that applicant has been granted interim order by this Court vide order dated 09.05.2022 in Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No.2583 of 2022.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No.2583 of 2022
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
In terms of the aforesaid interim order the applicant/ petitioners have cooperated in the investigation and after their proper co-operation charge sheet has been filed against present applicant and against Gajodhar, however,
final report has been filed against Ashok.

While granting interim protection the Division Bench of this Court has considered that FIR is a counter blast inasmuch as initially the petitioners' side had lodged an FIR against the husband of the victim and there was no iota of evidence justifying the involvement of the petitioner in commission of the offense.

6. Learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for the complainant have tried to justify the impugned FIR but could not dispute the aforesaid submissions of Shri Siddhartha Sinha, learned counsel for the applicant.

7. Having heard the arguments of learned counsel for the parties and having perused the material available on record and without entering into the merits of the issue, I find that the present applicant may be granted bail for the reason that the story and the allegations of the FIR could not be corroborated with the injury report, the complainant/ informant has changed the story at the stage of recording statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., there is no eye-witness account of the Vijay @ Vijay Kumar vs State Of U.P. therefore, final report has been filed in favour of Ashok and no protest application has been filed by the complainant and the fact that during course of investigation the applicant/ petitioner was granted interim protection by the Division Bench of this Court.

10. Let applicant- Vijay alias Vijay Kumar be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation,
then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law,
under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.
(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
(v) The applicant shall not leave India without previous permission of the court.
(Rajesh Singh Chauhan, J.) Order Date :- 15.4.2024
